title: Avocado vs. olive oil: fats and nutritional differences

seo.title: Avocado vs. olive oil: fat, calories and nutrition compared
seo.meta_description: Both are rich in monounsaturated fat, but avocado provides water and fiber while olive oil concentrates nearly all of its energy in fat. Compare realistic portions.
seo.search_intent: Compare avocado and olive oil by fat type, calories, fiber and practical nutritional role.

excerpt: Avocado and olive oil share a fat profile dominated by oleic acid, but they are not equivalent foods: 100 g of avocado provides about 160 calories, 15 g of fat and 6–7 g of fiber; one tablespoon of olive oil provides about 120 calories and 14 g of fat with virtually no fiber or protein. Avocado is a water-rich whole food; oil is concentrated fat.
content_html:
Avocado and olive oil are often grouped under the label “healthy fats,” which can make them sound interchangeable. They share one major feature—fat dominated by monounsaturated oleic acid—and differ on almost everything around that fat.

A useful comparison needs different serving sizes

One hundred grams of oil is not a normal serving. Comparing 100 g of avocado with one tablespoon of oil makes more sense because both are realistic amounts and their calorie totals are relatively close.

Avocado, 100 gOlive oil, 1 tbsp (14 g)
Calories~160~120
Total fat~15 g~14 g
Monounsaturated fat~10 g~10 g
Fiber~6.7 g0 g
Protein~2 g0 g
Water~73 gAlmost 0 g

The striking similarity is that both portions provide around 10 g of monounsaturated fat. The physical difference is just as large: 100 g of avocado is a much bigger volume of food.

Avocado carries fat inside a water- and fiber-rich matrix

Roughly three-quarters of avocado is water. Fiber and plant structure add chewing and volume, allowing about 15 g of fat to be spread through 100 g of food.

Oil has removed almost all of that structure and concentrates the lipid fraction. One tablespoon contains nearly as much total fat as 100 g of avocado.

Extra-virgin olive oil contains compounds not captured by macros

Virgin and extra-virgin olive oils contain phenolic compounds and vitamin E in varying amounts. Phenolic content depends on olive variety, maturity, processing and storage and is not usually shown on the standard Nutrition Facts panel.

Refining removes much of these minor compounds, so generic refined olive oil is not compositionally identical to extra-virgin olive oil.

Avocado brings fiber, folate and potassium

One hundred grams of avocado provides about 6–7 g of fiber and roughly 480 mg of potassium, plus folate and other micronutrients. Olive oil contains no fiber and negligible potassium.

That does not make avocado “better oil.” They serve different food roles.

For cooking, oil is much more functional

Oil coats pans, dresses vegetables and works as a cooking medium. Avocado adds texture and volume but cannot replace that technical function in most recipes.

If the goal is to replace butter or another more saturated cooking fat, olive oil directly shifts the recipe's fat profile toward monounsaturated fat.

Which one is lower in calories?

Per 100 g, avocado by a huge margin: around 160 calories versus about 884 in olive oil. But that comparison exaggerates normal use. One tablespoon of oil is about 120 calories; 100 g of avocado is about 160.

The amount used matters far more than the headline that oil has several times as many calories per 100 g.

The practical decision

Avocado and olive oil are complementary foods. Avocado delivers monounsaturated fat in a whole food with water, fiber and micronutrients; olive oil provides that fat in concentrated form and is especially useful for cooking, dressing and replacing more saturated fats.

faq.question: Which has more fat, avocado or olive oil?
faq.answer: Per 100 g, olive oil because it is nearly pure fat. But one tablespoon of oil contains about 14 g of fat, close to the 15 g in 100 g of avocado.

faq.question: Do avocado and olive oil contain the same type of fat?
faq.answer: Both are dominated by monounsaturated fat, especially oleic acid, although the foods around that fat are very different.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Avocado. One hundred grams provides about 6–7 g of fiber, while olive oil contains none.
